sentences.text: Shri Santosh Kumar Meena - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Bhaskar Agrawal - Govt. Advocate for the responden Heard on

I.A. No.15657/2025 which is first application under Section 430 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of suspension of remaining jail sentence filed on behalf of appellant - Kuwarsingh.

02. The appellant has been convicted under Section 344, 366, 376(2) (N) & 363 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.500/-, R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.500/-,
Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/-, R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.500/- & R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.500/- respectively and Section 5(L)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
2012 and sentenced to under Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/- respectively, with default stipulation.

sentences.text: 03. Counsel for the appellant argued that the appellant has already remained in jail for 5 years, this is an appeal of year 2022, therefore, final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
He further argued that the Prosecutrix was a consenting party and she had gone alongwith the present appellant and stayed for one month and 20 days with him.

He further argued that as per the prosecution, age of the Prosecutrix was 13 years 3 months and 20 days as per the scholar register,
but the prosecution has failed to prove the source on the basis of which the date of birth was recorded in the scholar 2 CRA-5888-2022 register.

In support of his contention, learned counsel has placed reliance on a judgment passed by the Division Bench in the case of Tejubai V/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75, in which it has been held that recording of the age of the prosecutrix cannot be the basis for conviction.

sentences.text: In such circumstances, his remaining jail sentence may be suspended.
04. Counsel for the respondent / State opposes the aforesaid application and prays for its rejection.

sentences.text:
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the testimony of the Prosecutrix that she was a consenting party and apart from that the source of age of the Prosecutrix has not been mentioned by the witnesses and also considering the judgment passed by the Division Bench in the case of Tejubai V/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75,
in which it has been held that recording of the age of the prosecutrix cannot be the basis for conviction and also considering that the appellant has already remained in jail for 5 years and this appeal is of year 2022, final hearing of this appeal will take time, we find prima facie case to grant suspension of jail sentence to the present appellant.
06.

entities.text: Tejubai V/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, I.A. No.15657/2025, is allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing fine amount and on furnishing personal bond by the appellant Kuwarsingh in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousands Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court and on deposit of fine amount (if not already deposited), the execution of custodial part of the jail sentence shall remain suspended, 3 CRA-5888-2022 till the final disposal of this appeal.

The appellant after being enlarged on bail, shall mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 04.08.2026 and on all such subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard.
Certified copy, as per rules.
(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) (ALOK AWA  JUDGE JUDGE
